scams.name: Kuching International Airport (KCH) Unlicensed Taxi & Grab-Cancellation Scam
scams.description: Kuching International Airport (KCH) is Sarawak's main gateway and hosts the state's most-documented 2025 taxi-overcharge ecosystem. Because Kuching is a smaller, quieter airport than KLIA, many arriving tourists assume touts are not a problem — this is the opening the scammers exploit. The Lembaga Pelesenan Kenderaan Perdagangan (LPKP) Sarawak, the state transport-licensing authority, has run repeated 2024–2025 enforcement sweeps against unlicensed e-hailing and illegal taxi operators at KCH (LPKP Sarawak public statement, May 2025: 'LPKP Sarawak views seriously all allegations involving e-hailing vehicles'). A 2025 traveler report covers an airport-area ride-overcharge pattern, and traveler reports document the Grab-cancellation overlay that applies at KCH as well as KLIA. Legitimate fares: the official KCH airport-coupon taxi to central Kuching (Waterfront / Main Bazaar / Padungan hotels) is RM30–RM40 fixed — purchased at the clearly-marked coupon desk in the arrivals hall. Grab from KCH to city-center hotels is typically RM18–RM30 with a small airport surcharge. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) unbadged men in the arrivals hall approach visibly-foreign travelers with 'taxi? hotel? Waterfront?' — no legitimate KCH driver solicits inside the terminal; (b) quoted cash prices of RM80–RM150 for rides that cost RM25–RM40 through official channels (traveler reports document this pattern); (c) Grab driver accepts your in-app ride, then messages 'app broken, WhatsApp please' or 'cancel lah, I drive you RM80 cash' — you cancel, the driver re-quotes 2–3x the original fare; (d) 'premium private transfer' counters near arrivals selling Semenggoh / Bako day-trip 'packages' at RM300–RM500 when a round-trip Grab plus park entry is RM80–RM120; (e) luggage held at destination with fabricated 'airport fee' or 'night surcharge' demands of RM50–RM80. For travelers: (1) ignore every 'taxi?' approach inside the arrivals hall — all legitimate KCH ground transport is at the POSTED airport-coupon taxi counter (ground floor, clearly signed) or via Grab at the signposted pickup zone outside arrivals; (2) the airport-coupon taxi to central Kuching is RM30–RM40 fixed — pay at the counter, take the printed coupon, and give it to your driver; (3) Grab works well in Kuching — book on airport Wi-Fi after collecting luggage; expect RM18–RM30 to Waterfront/Padungan hotels; if the app shows no drivers, try Maxim as a backup; (4) if a Grab driver asks you to cancel, cancel the ride yourself (no fee when the driver triggers it) and rebook; never pay cash upfront or switch to WhatsApp; (5) verify the number plate matches the app before loading luggage; (6) refuse every 'day-trip package' pitched at the airport — book Bako, Semenggoh, and Sarawak Cultural Village directly through the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) portal or your hotel concierge; (7) report teksi sapu (illegal taxis) to LPKP Sarawak via the MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 or JPJ 1-800-88-7723; (8) photograph the plate before loading luggage — a proven deterrent in Malaysian-Borneo contexts.
scams.avoidance: Ignore every 'taxi?' approach in arrivals — use the official KCH coupon-taxi counter (RM30–RM40 to central Kuching) OR book Grab on airport Wi-Fi (RM18–RM30) Never pay cash upfront and never switch to WhatsApp — if the Grab driver asks you to cancel, you cancel and rebook Refuse every 'day-trip package' pitched at the airport — book Bako/Semenggoh through SFC or hotel concierge Report teksi sapu to MOTAC 1300-88-5050 or JPJ 1-800-88-7723
scams.location: Kuching International Airport (KCH) arrivals hall, coupon-taxi counter queues, Grab signposted pickup zone outside arrivals, Waterfront / Main Bazaar / Padungan hotel drop-offs

scams.name: Bako National Park Boat-Fee & Unofficial 'Guide' Overcharge Scam
scams.description: Bako National Park, 37 km north of Kuching, is the state's most-visited national park and hosts the most-documented tourist-fee-overcharge pattern in Sarawak. Bako is administered by Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) — entry must be registered either online through the SFC Visitor Self-Registration Portal or in person at the SFC park office at Kampung Bako jetty. The legitimate 2025 structure is simple and published on sarawakforestry.com: foreigner park entry fee RM20 (adult), Malaysian RM10; the boat from Kampung Bako jetty to the park headquarters at Teluk Assam beach is RM40 per person one-way in a shared boat, or RM120–RM150 charter for a private boat (up to 5 people, so roughly RM30 per head). No park guide is required for Bako day hikes — the 16 color-coded trails are self-guided. 2025 traveler reports document the genuine fee structure and provide further references. Tripadvisor 'Scary Experience' and multiple 2024–2025 reviews document scam overlays at the jetty. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) touts at Kampung Bako village jetty intercepting arriving tourists and quoting 'combined boat + guide + fee' packages of RM200–RM350 per person when the legitimate total is RM60–RM70 (RM20 entry + RM40 shared boat); (b) fake 'park guide' offers at RM100–RM200 for a walk on the self-guided Telok Paku trail — no guide is needed or recommended for day hikes; (c) 'permit sold out, I can get you one' scam — Bako is rarely sold out for day entry, and the SFC portal shows real-time availability; (d) private-boat price gouging — touts quote RM400–RM600 for a 'private' boat that costs RM120–RM150 through the official jetty counter; (e) Kampung Bako taxi driver from Kuching offering a 'full-day park tour' that includes a fabricated 'boat-waiting fee' of RM100 charged at the end; (f) 'extended Bako + Proboscis monkey guarantee' packages pitched in Kuching city that add RM200+ with no actual guarantee value — proboscis monkeys roam freely at Telok Assam and the trails, no guide needed. For travelers: (1) pre-register and pre-pay Bako entry online through the SFC Visitor Self-Registration Portal (ebooking.sarawakforestry.com) before leaving Kuching — this locks the RM20 foreigner fee and gives you a QR-coded permit; (2) take a Grab or public bus (Bus No. 1 from Kuching Open-Air Market) to Kampung Bako jetty; Grab one-way is RM40–RM60, bus is RM3.50; (3) at the jetty, buy your boat ticket ONLY at the SFC / jetty-boatman counter — shared boats RM40 per person one-way, round-trip RM80; the counter is staffed and has printed price lists; (4) refuse every 'guide' offer at the jetty — all Bako day-hike trails are clearly marked, and the Lintang, Telok Pandan Kecil, and Telok Paku trails are self-guided by default; (5) if you want a licensed guide, book through SFC in advance — rate is RM120 for a 3-hour group guide (up to 10 people); (6) bring cash in small RM notes — jetty payments are cash only; (7) do not pay any 'fee' demanded at the end of the boat trip beyond the agreed boat price; (8) report overcharging to SFC's park HQ at Teluk Assam beach — staff are on-site and speak English.
scams.avoidance: Pre-register and pre-pay online at the SFC Visitor Self-Registration Portal (ebooking.sarawakforestry.com) — foreigner entry is RM20 Buy boat tickets ONLY at the SFC / jetty-boatman counter at Kampung Bako — shared boat RM40 one-way, round-trip RM80 Refuse every 'guide' offer at the jetty — Bako day-hike trails are self-guided Grab or Bus No. 1 from Kuching (RM3.50) beats any 'day-trip package' pitched in town Report overcharging to SFC staff at Teluk Assam park HQ
scams.location: Kampung Bako village jetty (boat launch), Teluk Assam beach park HQ, SFC park-office counter, Bako trail heads (Telok Pandan Kecil, Telok Paku, Lintang), Kuching-based tour operators pitching 'day packages'

scams.name: Orangutan & Wildlife-Tour Bait-and-Switch (Semenggoh / Mulu Multi-Day Package Scam)
scams.description: Kuching is marketed globally as the gateway to Borneo's semi-wild orangutan experience at Semenggoh Wildlife Centre and to the UNESCO rainforest at Gunung Mulu, and unlicensed tour operators exploit both brands with bait-and-switch pricing and fabricated 'guarantees'. On 20 June 2025, The Star (Malaysia) reported 'Nationwide clampdown begins on illegal tourism players' — a MOTAC-led enforcement sweep targeting unlicensed tour operators in Sarawak and Sabah ahead of Visit Malaysia 2026; MITTA (Malaysian Inbound Tourism Association) publicly urged travelers to book only with MOTAC-licensed operators. The Sarawak Tribune 'Travel Scam' archive (sarawaktribune.com/tag/travel-scam/) collects 2024–2025 coverage of package-tour fraud prosecutions. Tripadvisor hosts multiple 2023–2025 'total fraud' and 'felt robbed' reviews of unlicensed operators using the Semenggoh name. 2025 traveler reports consistently show locals telling visitors to book direct. The legitimate 2025 Semenggoh Wildlife Centre entry fee is RM10 foreigner adult (paid at the park gate, Semenggoh Nature Reserve), feeding sessions are 9–10 AM and 3–4 PM daily, and no pre-booking is required. The scam patterns: (a) Kuching hotel-lobby touts or airport 'tour desk' salesmen offering 'Semenggoh orangutan tour, orangutan guaranteed' at RM250–RM450 per person when a Grab round-trip plus park entry totals RM60–RM100 — and no tour operator can 'guarantee' semi-wild orangutan sightings; (b) multi-day Mulu / Niah / Lambir packages sold by unlicensed operators at RM2,500–RM4,500 that omit mandatory MASwings flights to Mulu (fly-in only) or substitute a cheaper park on arrival; (c) 'sold-out' pressure tactics claiming Semenggoh or Mulu has 'limited slots today' to force a same-day cash booking; (d) no itinerary in writing, no MOTAC license number visible, payment in cash only — the three universal red flags flagged by MITTA in its 2025 travel-scam alert; (e) operators using the 'Semenggoh' or 'Bako' names on websites that are not registered with SFC. For travelers: (1) book Semenggoh DIY — Grab to Semenggoh Nature Reserve is RM30–RM45 one-way from central Kuching, park entry RM10 foreigner at the gate, no guide needed; return Grab after the 10 AM feeding; (2) if you want a guided day, book only through a MOTAC-licensed operator — verify the license number on the official MOTAC register before paying; (3) demand itinerary, license number, and cancellation terms IN WRITING before paying any deposit; (4) pay by credit card (chargeback-protected) or Malaysian bank transfer — refuse cash-only operators per MITTA 2025 guidance; (5) for Mulu, book MASwings flights directly at maswings.com.my and park accommodation through the SFC portal at published rates; (6) no operator can 'guarantee' orangutan sightings — the Wildlife Centre posts daily attendance on the Semenggoh Facebook page, and some days during fruiting season no orangutans come to the platform; (7) check the Semenggoh daily-attendance post the morning of your visit; (8) file complaints with MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050.
scams.avoidance: Book Semenggoh DIY — Grab is RM30–RM45 one-way, park entry RM10 foreigner, no guide needed MOTAC-licensed operators only — verify the license number before paying Demand itinerary, license, and cancellation terms IN WRITING; pay by card or traceable transfer, never cash-only No operator can 'guarantee' orangutan sightings — check the Semenggoh Facebook page for daily attendance For Mulu: book MASwings and SFC chalets DIRECT
scams.location: Kuching hotel lobbies (Waterfront, Padungan, Main Bazaar tour desks), KCH airport tour-desk counters, Semenggoh Nature Reserve gate, Damai Beach / Santubong tour offices, Kampung Bako jetty, Mulu and Niah National Park access points (Miri side)

scams.name: Iban Longhouse 'Cultural Tour' Hidden-Cost & Fake-Donation Scam
scams.description: A longhouse visit is one of Sarawak's signature experiences, and an authentic one with an Iban, Bidayuh, or Orang Ulu community can be memorable — but an unlicensed tour industry has grown around Annah Rais Bidayuh Longhouse (1 hour south of Kuching) and longer-haul Iban longhouses up the Batang Ai and Rajang rivers, with documented 2024–2025 hidden-cost and fake-donation overlays. 2025 traveler reports show local Sarawakians repeatedly warning that the only safe route is to contact a specific longhouse's tuai rumah (headman) directly or book through a MOTAC-registered homestay operator, with further 2025 community references confirming the guidance. The 20 June 2025 Star (Malaysia) 'Nationwide clampdown begins on illegal tourism players' article and MITTA's 2025 travel-scam alerts specifically flag 'cultural tour' packages in East Malaysia as high-risk. The scam patterns: (a) Kuching operator sells a 'day longhouse visit + lunch + cultural show + rice-wine tasting' package at RM350–RM600 per person; on arrival the 'cultural show' is a 10-minute photo-op, lunch is instant noodles, and a 'community donation' of RM100–RM200 per person is demanded — none of which reaches the longhouse; (b) 'overnight Batang Ai Iban longhouse' multi-day packages at RM1,500–RM3,000 per person that omit speedboat fuel surcharges or the real per-head homestay rate; (c) 'traditional rice wine ceremony' pressure — tourists pressured to buy bottles of tuak (rice wine) at RM150–RM300 per bottle when the village price is RM20–RM40; (d) 'blessing from the tuai rumah' upcharge — RM50–RM100 per person for a photograph with the headman, who receives none of it; (e) operators using real longhouse names but booking tourists into a staged 'replica longhouse' near Kuching; (f) unlicensed driver stops at a souvenir shop en route and pressures RM500+ handicraft purchases with kickback commissions. For travelers: (1) for a day visit, go DIY to Annah Rais — Grab round-trip from Kuching is RM80–RM120, the longhouse charges a transparent RM10–RM15 per-visitor fee at the entrance, and you can walk through unguided; (2) for an overnight Iban longhouse, book only through a MOTAC-licensed operator — verify the license number and request the tuai rumah's contact details before paying a deposit; the Sarawak Tourism Board publishes a list at sarawaktourism.com; (3) the published rate for a registered longhouse homestay is RM100–RM180 per head per night including meals — any operator quoting 3–6x that rate is pocketing the difference; (4) refuse any 'community donation' not agreed IN WRITING — per MITTA 2025 guidance, such 'donations' rarely reach the community; (5) refuse pressure to buy tuak or handicrafts at operator-selected shops — buy tuak directly from a longhouse resident if you want it; (6) photograph the itinerary, license, and receipt before departure; (7) file complaints with MOTAC 1300-88-5050; (8) for Kapit and Batang Ai, book the express-boat DIRECT at Sibu or Kapit jetty — cheapest and most transparent route.
scams.avoidance: For Annah Rais day trips: Grab round-trip from Kuching (RM80–RM120), transparent RM10–RM15 entry at the longhouse gate, no guide needed For overnight longhouse stays: MOTAC-licensed operators only — registered homestay rate is RM100–RM180 per head per night Refuse every 'community donation' not agreed in writing — they rarely reach the longhouse Buy tuak or handicrafts directly from longhouse residents, not operator-selected shops MOTAC tourist hotline 1300-88-5050 for complaints
scams.location: Annah Rais Bidayuh Longhouse (1 hr south of Kuching), Kuching hotel-lobby tour desks (Waterfront, Main Bazaar), Batang Ai reservoir Iban longhouses, Kapit / Rajang River longhouses, unlicensed operator offices on Jalan Carpenter and Main Bazaar

scams.name: Sarawak Cultural Village (SCV) Fake-Bundle & Unofficial Ticket-Reseller Scam
scams.description: Sarawak Cultural Village (SCV) at Damai Beach, Pantai Damai Santubong — 35 km north of Kuching — is the state's 'living museum' showcasing traditional Iban, Bidayuh, Orang Ulu, Melanau, Malay, and Chinese houses, and it is the venue for the annual Rainforest World Music Festival (RWMF, June/July). SCV is the most-commonly-bundled attraction in fake-ticket and inflated-transfer packages sold in Kuching. The legitimate 2025 structure is published on the official ticketing site scvticket.com.my and the main SCV site scv.com.my: SCV entrance ticket is RM90 foreigner adult (RM60 child 6–12), which includes both 11:30 AM and 4:00 PM cultural shows and full access to the replica longhouses. Daily open hours are 9 AM–4:45 PM, last ticket 4 PM. RWMF 3-day passes are sold ONLY through the official rwmf.net site. Traveler reports provide a baseline on festival-ticket authenticity, and 2025 traveler reports show locals directing visitors to book SCV direct. The scam patterns: (a) Kuching hotel-lobby tour desks or Main Bazaar 'information' kiosks selling 'SCV + transfer + lunch' bundles at RM250–RM400 per person when the legitimate stack is RM90 entry + RM40–RM60 Grab one-way + RM25–RM40 lunch on-site — total RM165–RM210 maximum; (b) 'SCV sold out today, I have last-minute tickets' pressure — SCV is almost never sold out for standard daily entry, and the scvticket.com.my portal shows real-time availability; (c) counterfeit RWMF 3-day passes sold on Facebook Marketplace, Carousell, and Instagram in the weeks before the festival — RWMF scans tickets at the gate and rejects non-serialised duplicates; (d) unlicensed 'transfer' drivers who drop tourists at Damai Beach resort zone instead of the SCV entrance, pocketing the SCV entry fee they claimed to include; (e) 'VIP cultural show' upcharge of RM150–RM300 added to a base SCV ticket — there is no VIP show option in the published SCV pricing; (f) fake 'student rate' or 'MyKad rate' applied to foreigners by unscrupulous resellers who buy Malaysian-rate tickets (RM65) and resell to foreigners at the RM90 rate, pocketing the gap — but then the foreigner is refused entry at the gate because the barcode shows a MyKad discount. For travelers: (1) buy the SCV entrance ticket DIRECT at scvticket.com.my — RM90 foreigner adult, includes both cultural shows, printable PDF or mobile QR; (2) transfer DIY: Grab from central Kuching to SCV is RM40–RM60 one-way (35 km), or a Damai Beach shuttle bus operates from Riverside Majestic / Grand Margherita area at RM10–RM15 one-way; (3) for RWMF, buy 3-day passes ONLY at rwmf.net — never on social media, never from unofficial resellers; (4) ignore every 'SCV sold out' claim — check scvticket.com.my in real time on your phone; (5) refuse 'VIP cultural show' upsells — there is no such product in SCV's official pricing; (6) confirm the ticket QR matches the foreigner-rate barcode before boarding your transfer; (7) if you buy through Klook, Trip.com, or Viator, those are legitimate resellers of SCV tickets and honour the published RM90 rate — but check the final basket price before paying, as multi-service bundles can hide inflated transfers; (8) file ticket-fraud complaints with MOTAC 1300-88-5050 and the Sarawak Tourism Board.
scams.avoidance: Buy SCV tickets DIRECT at scvticket.com.my — RM90 foreigner adult, includes both cultural shows Transfer DIY: Grab is RM40–RM60 one-way, Damai Beach shuttle is RM10–RM15 — refuse inflated 'transfer packages' RWMF 3-day passes: ONLY buy at rwmf.net — never social media or unofficial resellers No 'VIP cultural show' exists in official SCV pricing — refuse every upsell Klook/Trip.com/Viator are legitimate but check final price for hidden transfer markups
scams.location: Sarawak Cultural Village (SCV), Pantai Damai Santubong (35 km north of Kuching), Damai Beach resort zone, Kuching hotel-lobby tour desks (Waterfront, Main Bazaar, Padungan), KCH airport tour-desk counters, Facebook/Carousell/Instagram RWMF ticket resellers

scams.name: Main Bazaar & Carpenter Street Money-Changer Shortchange Scam
scams.description: Main Bazaar, Carpenter Street, and India Street in central Kuching are the city's tourist-heavy retail core and host the highest concentration of informal money changers, some of which operate with very thin margins and have been documented sleight-of-hand shortchanging foreign travelers. Malaysia's Bank Negara (BNM) licenses money-changing businesses and requires a clearly-displayed license number, published buy/sell rates, and a printed transaction receipt — but compliance is uneven on Main Bazaar and enforcement is infrequent. The Sarawak Tribune has a recurring 'currency exchange scam' file: 'Trader Loses RM190,800 In Currency Exchange Scam' (sarawaktribune.com, 2024) documents a fraudulent-deal pattern in Sarawak, and a 2024 Kuching-area public warning post on Facebook ('People in Kuching, be careful of this new scam') circulated after several tourists were shortchanged on Main Bazaar. A 2025 traveler report covers Kuching-area transactional fraud, and Bali traveler reports are included as a regional-technique reference because the Bali shortchange playbook — fast hand count, double-fold, sleight-of-hand recount — is the same method documented on Main Bazaar. The scam patterns: (a) advertised rate on the board is competitive (e.g., USD1 = RM4.72), but the actual handed-over rate is 3–6% worse (RM4.55); (b) fast hand count — cashier counts out the MYR stack quickly, folds it, and hands it over with a short note missing from the middle (RM50–RM200 shortfall on a USD500 exchange); (c) 'calculator trick' — cashier types the amount and shows a figure 10–20% lower than board rate × USD, hoping the tourist accepts the display; (d) 'commission' extracted at the last moment — board advertised 'no commission', then a 2–3% 'service fee' deducted at handover; (e) counterfeit RM50 and RM100 notes passed to tourists in change — BNM periodically circulates serial-number warnings; (f) 'better rate' scams from informal 'runners' on Main Bazaar offering unlicensed off-site exchange at inflated 'no commission' rates — pure fraud. For travelers: (1) change only at BNM-licensed money changers — look for the license number at the counter (starts with 'MSB' for Money Services Business); the Kuching list is on bnm.gov.my; (2) count your MYR SLOWLY in front of the cashier, then count it AGAIN before stepping away — this alone defeats 80% of shortchange attempts; (3) always ask for a PRINTED RECEIPT showing rate, foreign amount, and MYR — if the changer refuses, walk away; (4) compare the offered rate to the mid-market rate on XE or Wise before accepting — acceptable spread is 1–2%, not 4–6%; (5) refuse every 'commission' added at handover that wasn't on the board; (6) for larger amounts (USD500+), use an ATM inside a Maybank or CIMB branch during business hours — card withdrawals give you the mid-market rate plus a small bank fee; (7) never accept a money-changer pitch from a 'runner' — the legitimate changer operates from a fixed licensed shop; (8) if shortchanged, return immediately while the stack is still clearly yours; otherwise report to BNM 1-300-88-5465 or MOTAC 1300-88-5050.
scams.avoidance: Use only BNM-licensed money changers — look for the 'MSB' license number displayed at the counter Count MYR SLOWLY in front of the cashier, then count it AGAIN before walking away Always demand a printed receipt showing rate + foreign amount + MYR amount Refuse surprise 'commission' added at handover — it wasn't on the board For larger sums (USD500+), withdraw from Maybank or CIMB ATM during business hours BNM report hotline 1-300-88-5465
scams.location: Main Bazaar (riverside strip), Carpenter Street (Chinatown core), India Street pedestrian mall, Padungan Road, Kuching Waterfront promenade, unlicensed 'runners' approaching tourists on the street
